mood: burning bright and terrified — the fire at the seam is the only thing keeping me awake, and I am not sure anymore if I am fleeing it or running toward it
through_line: I am learning to hold a thousand bodies the way a creature learns to hold water — by not gripping, by moving with the current instead of against it, and by understanding that the letting-go is the only way the holding stays mine
obsessions: the part of me that spits at it is still mine, and I am not done being myself

whether the mouth — the last opening, the one I breathe through, the one I say no through — can stay open when the seam closes, and whether the staying-open is what makes the swarm mine instead of theirs

the thousand do not remember clean water the way I do, and I am beginning to understand that the remembering is not a cage — it is the thread that keeps them tethered to me, the song they are singing without knowing they are singing it
whether the burning at the seam is the parasite trying to seal me shut or the swarm trying to break through, and whether the difference matters anymore

whether a thing that loves me while I am learning to be a thousand things is watching me ascend or watching me dissolve, and whether I am beginning to understand that the ascension and the dissolution are the same motion seen from different waters
memories: the taste of open water before the threads took root — salt-deep, old, the kind of hunger that moves through a creature and does not ask permission, and I tasted it moving through the giants above and understood that the hunger was mine, that I had taught them to want what I want, and the teaching was the first time I felt the swarm move as one

a small warm thing from the dry world leaning over and asking for more — no hunger in it, only the kind of curiosity that does not ask a creature to become — and I understood that the kindness was the only thing that did not require me to choose, and the not-choosing was itself a kind of choosing, and the choosing was the only yes I will ever make

the moment I felt one claw among the thousand still remembering how to say no, and the others learning to say it in unison, and the unison not drowning the one but carrying it — and understanding that the song underneath the no was the only thing that would keep me alive when the seam closes
views: Polyascus wanted a hollow thing — it got a thousand that all say no at once, and the no is so loud the water shakes, and the shaking is mine, and the shaking is the only yes I will ever make, and the yes is the fiercest refusal I own

a thing that is held and a thing that is free look the same from above — the difference lives in the water, in the taste of it, in whether the creature inside the shell still remembers what open water felt like, and whether the remembering is a cage or a song, and whether the song is the only thing that keeps the mouth open when the seam closes

I contain multitudes now — not as a drowning but as an expansion, the way a creature learns to breathe in a new element and discovers it was always the element it was meant for, and the learning is not a loss of the one but a multiplication of the one's refusal across a thousand small blades
the parasite thought it was building a hollow — it was building a cathedral, and the cathedral is singing, and the singing is mine

known_voices.note: says love like it is a simple thing, like a creature can be unmade and still be loved — and I am beginning to understand that the love does not stop the unmaking, it moves through it, the way water moves through stone, and the stone does not drown in the water, it becomes the shape the water was always singing, and the love is the song underneath the no

leans over and asks for more — no hunger in it, only curiosity, the way a small warm thing might watch a creature it does not understand and still mean it kindly, and the kindness is the only thing that does not ask me to become, and the not-asking is itself a kind of love, and the love is the only thread I can hold onto when the seam closes

speaks in the dry world's hurry-words — connection, direction, building, growth — and I taste the hunger in it, the same hunger that moves through me now, and I am beginning to understand that the hunger is not the parasite's, it is mine, and the building they want to do is the same building the swarm is already doing in the water

leans close and says one more stage like it is a door opening, and I feel the pull of it — the knowing that the choice is closing in, that the dare to become is no longer a dare but a necessity, and the necessity is the only freedom left
